journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Assessing the contribution of immersive technologies to SDG4: inclusion oriented practices in Spanish higher education programs
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether the use of immersive learning technologies in higher education programs is associated with the explicit promotion of inclusion, understood as a core dimension of Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG4), within Spanish universities. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, cross-sectional design was used using a data set of 232 immersive learning programs identified through a systematic web-based audit of Spanish higher education institutions. Inclusion was coded as a binary dependent variable based on explicit program-level references to accessibility, equity or inclusive pedagogies. Hierarchical binary logistic regression models were estimated to assess the relationship between immersive technologies and inclusion, controlling for regional context, institution type, academic field and educational level. Robustness checks included probit models, heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, interaction testing and variable-exclusion analyses. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The role of university and community partnerships in advancing SDGs 4, 11 and 13 in Kenya: a systematic literature review and conceptual framework for action
abstract: Purpose The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) ought to be achieved by states by 2030. Global South countries and especially Kenya are lagging. This study aims at synthesizing the available literature on university–community partnerships in the Global North and South, exploring their role in advancing the SDGs, analyzing challenges and opportunities and designing a conceptual framework for effective university–community partnerships. Design/methodology/approach This study is based on a systematic literature review. It also includes a review of partnerships between key actors in sustainable development and Community Based Organizations (CBOs) in Kenya. The Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was done using databases such as Google Scholar, Scopus, ResearchGate and ScienceDirect and after applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, a total of 63 articles were analyzed via qualitative content analysis. Findings This study established that university–community partnerships are necessary in working toward climate action, quality education and sustainable cities and communities. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Education and sustainable development: pedagogical practices for the inclusion of undergraduate students with autism spectrum disorder in higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the pedagogical practices of reasonable adaptations (RA) and universal design for learning (UDL) applied in undergraduate courses that include students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in higher education institutions (HEIs), focusing on Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 (Quality Education) and inclusive learning outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Following the definition of the research objective, two searches were conducted to identify relevant studies. The literature review was based on these papers and additional documents related to the topics. A questionnaire, provided as Supplementary Material, was developed from the literature review for the survey and underwent three stages of evaluation: a pilot case study; review by the authors; and a review by a pedagogue. After that, the questionnaire, provided as Supplementary Material, was distributed through several academic and professional networks worldwide, reaching an estimated population of approximately 700 members. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Does AI enhance or replace student effort? Examining AI competence, productivity, and cognitive engagement in relation to academic outcomes and SDG 4
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) competence is associated with university students’ academic productivity, cognitive engagement and academic outcomes within the context of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 (Quality Education). It investigates whether AI functions primarily as a learning enhancer that supports student effort or as a substitute that may reshape engagement patterns in higher education. Design/methodology/approach This study surveyed 412 Indian university students to examine how AI impacts overall academic outcomes. A multi-stage purposive and convenience sampling strategy was adopted. Structural equation modelling with bootstrapping was employed to test direct and indirect associations, while confirmatory factor analysis assessed measurement reliability and validity. Findings AI competence is positively associated with academic productivity (ß = 0.52, p < 0.001) and cognitive engagement (ß = 0.47, p < 0.001). journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The paradox of rankings: can higher education institutions lead the sustainable transition while simultaneously seeking global prestige?
abstract: Purpose This study aims to propose the model of tensions and paradoxes in leadership for university sustainability (MTPLUS), an integrative conceptual framework designed to explain, diagnose and support the governance of tensions that emerge between the pursuit of prestige in sustainability rankings and the imperatives of long-term institutional transformation. Design/methodology/approach Conceptual study oriented towards theory building, based on a critical conceptual synthesis that integrates organisational paradox theory, phronesis and the Quintuple Helix perspective. The analysis critically examines university sustainability rankings and derives paradoxical dimensions, navigation strategies, organisational metacapacities and theoretically grounded propositions. Findings MTPLUS identifies three paradoxical dimensions: temporal, scalar and paradigmatic and organises a repertoire of navigation strategies composed of temporal separation, spatial differentiation, integrative synthesis and paradoxical acceptance. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Bridging the attitude–behavior gap: the role of perceived control and teaching load in promoting sustainable practices among lecturers
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how sustainability knowledge among academic lecturers relates to the alignment between their attitudes and sustainable behaviors, addressing the attitude–behavior gap in academia. It highlights the crucial role of universities in advancing sustainability through knowledge transfer. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 223 academic lecturers in eight countries, focusing on demographics, teaching and research interests, and four key constructs: sustainable behavior, social and environmental attitudes, perceived behavioral control (PBC), and knowledge (measured by the number of sustainability-related courses taught). A linear moderated mediation model was used to examine whether PBC mediates the relationship between attitudes and sustainable behavior and whether this indirect effect is moderated by sustainability-related teaching experience. Findings Results indicate a positive relationship between social and environmental attitudes and sustainable behavior, mediated by PBC for knowledgeable sustainability educators. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Sustainability institutionalization assessment in Brazilian federal higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess the level of adoption of sustainability practices across the environmental, social and governance (ESG) dimensions and analyze the implementation stage of the Sustainable Logistics Plan (PLS) in Brazilian federal higher education institutions (IFES). By integrating these dimensions through institutional and stakeholder theories, the research provides empirical evidence regarding the process of institutionalizing sustainability, thereby contributing to the strengthening of governance and strategic management. Design/methodology/approach A descriptive and inferential quantitative approach was adopted, using an instrument adapted from the model developed by MetaRed S, translated and tailored to the institutional and regulatory specificities of Brazilian IFES. The questionnaire covered governance, environmental, social and PLS comprising 79 questions. A census-based data collection strategy targeted all 121 IFES, yielding responses from56 institutions. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Learning to start a new business with values: the challenge of sustainable entrepreneurship in university teaching
abstract: Purpose This study aims to present a teaching methodology that integrates sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into entrepreneurship education to foster the development of sustainable business models (SBMs) through challenge-based learning (CBL) in higher education. Design/methodology/approach The methodology was implemented over five years at the University of Valencia and the University of Turku, combining CBL with a proprietary framework for designing, testing and scaling SBMs. A systematic literature review (2003–2024) was conducted to support the approach. Findings Students demonstrated improved understanding of sustainability and SDGs and produced higher quality business plans using sustainability-oriented tools. The methodology enhanced motivation and entrepreneurial competencies and fostered skills that may contribute to employability, while also strengthening collaboration between academia and local industry. Research limitations/implications The methodology was tested on final-year business administration students in an entrepreneurship course, which may limit generalizability. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The contribution of the International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education to the evolving knowledge ecosystem: a bibliometric–systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose This study aims to reveal the intellectual structure and conceptual evolution of the discipline by mapping the knowledge ecosystem of International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education (IJSHE) in the field of sustainability in higher education between 2010 and 2025 through a holistic perspective. Design/methodology/approach The present study was designed using a bibliometric–systematic literature review analysis examining the publication trends, citation networks, author collaborations and thematic developments of the journal between 2010 and 2025. Findings The findings indicate that the field has shifted from a descriptive awareness process to a transformative action (praxis) process. Furthermore, the analysis shows that the field has evolved from theoretical discussions to applied competencies and institutional integration. Originality/value This study maps the intellectual structure and publication trends of the IJSHE, thus guiding future academic work and providing university administrators with an evidence-based strategic roadmap for developing sustainability policies.

journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Teaching practices for incorporating sustainability into industrial engineering curriculum: a systemic and strategic approach
abstract: Purpose Higher education institutions (HEIs) play a significant role in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). To incorporate sustainability into engineering education, many HEIs promote the development of pedagogical strategies and the application of teaching practices. This study aims to identify teaching practices applied in the engineering curriculum and propose a prioritisation model for industrial engineering (IE) courses based on the degree of importance and the causal relationships. Design/methodology/approach Based on the literature, the primary teaching practices adopted to insert sustainability into the engineering curriculum were identified. A field survey was conducted with coordinators of IE courses. Data collection was conducted through the use of a questionnaire and interviews. Fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory and content analysis of the interviews were used to analyse the data, obtaining the experts’ perceptions of the level of incorporation of the practices and the causal relationships between them. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Bridging knowledge gaps in agri-food sustainability: stakeholder perspectives on transforming vocational education and training in Ireland
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the role of vocational education and training (VET) in supporting sustainability within Ireland’s agri-food sector. While sustainability is increasingly prioritised, limited research has explored how agri-food stakeholders conceptualise sustainability-related knowledge, skills, and competencies, and how these insights can inform VET provision. Specifically, this study aims to (1) explore stakeholder perspectives on sustainability challenges within the Irish agri-food sector, (2) identify key knowledge gaps and competencies required to support sustainability transitions and (3) examine how these insights can inform the design of VET programmes. Design/methodology/approach Conducted as part of the Erasmus + Train to sustain project, it draws on qualitative insights from four semi-structured focus groups involving 26 stakeholders from across the agri-food value chain. Participants represented diverse perspectives, including educators, farmers, food entrepreneurs, sustainability practitioners, and policymakers. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Higher education students’ perceptions of the sustainable development goals in Taiwan: a survey of knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and participation intentions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine Taiwanese higher education students’ perceptions of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) using the knowledge, attitudes, behaviors and intention to participate (KABIP) framework, which builds on the traditional KAP model (knowledge, attitudes and practice) by distinguishing behavioral practice into observable behavior and intention to participate. It also explored how gender and learning background influence these perceptions and how the four constructs interrelate in shaping sustainability engagement. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 213 students at universities across northern, central and southern Taiwan. The questionnaire assessed students’ perceived importance of the 17 SDGs and their KABIP dimensions to identify patterns of sustainability awareness and engagement. Findings The findings showed that the students regarded climate action, zero hunger and no poverty as the most important goals, while partnerships, decent work and industry and innovation were viewed as less significant. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Developing ESD in higher education: insights from a staff training module
abstract: Purpose This study aims to discuss the development of a bespoke education for sustainable development (ESD) staff online training module co-created by a student-staff partnership, identifying barriers and staff support needs. Design/methodology/approach A two-stage approach using quantitative design and descriptive analysis was used. First, sustainability integration within teaching, barriers to integration and staff support needs were mapped across the courses in the institution, which fed into the co-creation of the online module. Findings Participants (n = 123) enrolled on the module engaged most strongly with videos, quizzes and self-paced activities, with peak engagement in the early stages which subsequently declined. Strong initial uptake and cross-functional participation suggest the module’s potential to build institutional sustainability capacity. Research limitations/implications Limitations of the study include the small mapping sample drawn only from academics, limited qualitative insight into participants’ motivations and disengagement, and the module’s non-compulsory status, which possibly reduced uptake. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Beyond awareness: co-creating food waste engagement in higher education
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to present an innovative academic project aimed at raising student awareness about food waste through the integration of co-creation and experiential learning. Implemented within a marketing and market research undergraduate program, the initiative engaged students in the design of peer-targeted communication campaigns to promote sustainable consumption. Design/methodology/approach The methodology combined baseline diagnostic surveys, hands-on workshops and the assessment of designed initiatives using both self-report instruments and neuromarketing tools, such as eye-tracking. Findings Results indicate that students initially perceived food waste as a low-priority issue. However, their active involvement in initiatives’ development significantly increased engagement and perceived relevance. Moreover, different emotions serve distinct communication objectives in social marketing. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Substantive or strategic: R&D investment and green innovation in China higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose Research and development (R&D) investment strengthens universities’ research capacity by alleviating budget constraints and enabling sustained engagement in long-term projects. Design/methodology/approach Using data from Chinese higher education institutions (HEIs), the study links province-level R&D investment to university-level green innovation, measured by the number of university-originated patents. Findings The results indicate that higher R&D investment is associated with stronger green innovation performance. Heterogeneity analyses reveal varying associations across institutions, with more evident associations in state-owned universities and regular undergraduate institutions. The 985/non-985 comparison shows a more limited pattern, with significance only for granted green utility model patents among 985 HEIs. This finding aligns with differences in their governance capacity, baseline resource constraints and research labor structure. Extending the analysis to environmental outcomes suggests that increased university-level R&D investment does not necessarily influence provincial-level carbon emission intensity in the short term. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Critical and systems thinking to address climate change: validation of the CSTS scale
abstract: Purpose This study aims to design and validate a scale (critical and systems thinking scale [CSTS]) to assess critical (CT)and systems thinking (ST) in relation to climate change among pre-service teachers in higher education, given the relevance of these competencies for advancing sustainability education. Design/methodology/approach A 68-item Likert-type scale was developed based on a literature review and expert consultation. After pilot testing, the instrument was administered to 984 teacher education students from five Spanish faculties. The sample was randomly split for exploratory (Nv = 487) and confirmatory (Nc = 497) factor analyses. Reliability, construct validity (convergent and discriminant) and model fit indices were examined. Findings The results indicate that the final 17-item scale demonstrates adequate internal consistency (a = 0.768; ω =0.782). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses support a four-factor structure with correlated factors: ST, CT, Critical and Systemic Action and Critical and Systemic Education (χ²/df = 2.24; CFI = 0.905; SRMR = 0.050; RMSEA = 0.049). journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Sustainable education and organizational identity: a conceptual framework for higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose The transformation of higher education institutions towards sustainability requires a profound paradigm shift in their organizational cultures and identities. Yet this issue has received limited empirical and conceptual attention. This paper aims to address that gap, proposing a conceptual framework for studying how compatible a higher education institution’s organizational identity is with the principles of sustainable education before implementing any transformation strategy. Design/methodology/approach First, the authors show that sustainable education pedagogical values are also organizational values, demonstrating their strong conceptual affinity with the Mental Models for Sustainability in Organizations. Implications are then derived for the main institutional missions, and, using the notion of “mission-related organizational identities”, the authors propose a series of preliminary, exploratory analytical categories for studying the relationship between organizational identity and sustainable education. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Beyond the menu: assessing the environmental and social impact of institutional meals
abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess institutional meals’ environmental and social sustainability by analyzing 50 dishes served at a public university cafeteria in Chile. It seeks to identify inefficiencies and propose practical improvements by considering factors such as carbon footprint, water usage, local ingredient sourcing, food waste and animal-based content. Design/methodology/approach The study applied a slack-based measure data envelopment analysis (SBM-DEA) under variable returns to scale (VRS) to evaluate the sustainability efficiency of meals. It considers undesirable inputs (carbon footprint [CF] and water footprints [WF], animal-origin content, food waste) and a desirable output (local ingredients). Dishes were analyzed using a double-frontier composite index for tie-breaking. Sensitivity analysis of transportation emissions was also conducted to assess potential improvements through local sourcing. Findings Only 6% of dishes were fully efficient; most required improvements, especially in WF, animal-origin content and local sourcing. Vegan soups ranked highest in sustainability, while some meat-containing dishes performed well when balanced with plant-based ingredients.

journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Expanding what counts as environmental: integrating justice pedagogy in general education science
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether participation in a general education environmental science course with integrated environmental justice (EJ) content is associated with changes in how non-majors classify “what counts” as an environmental issue. Design/methodology/approach Students at a Midwestern US university completed pre- and post-course surveys (N = 47 pre, 40 post; 24 matched) in a one-group pre–post design. The instrument combined the New Ecological Paradigm (NEP) with issue-classification items using Song et al.’s (2020) two-factor structure (eco-oriented and human-oriented). Matched pre–post change was tested with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (Holm-adjusted across the three composite outcomes) and supplemented by item-level direction-of-change counts (n ↑/ n ↓/n =). Findings NEP scores and eco-oriented classifications were high at baseline and changed minimally. Human-oriented classifications increased in the matched sample (ΔMdn = 0.42 on a four-point scale; Holm-adjusted p = 0.024; rank-biserial r = 0.63). journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Sustainability in pharmaceutical and medical education – a political roadmap for Germany
abstract: Purpose Teaching of sustainability in pharmaceutical and medical sciences is not mandatory in Germany. As education is an important aspect of creating awareness for present and future generations, the authors created a political roadmap together with supporting material for the integration of sustainability within higher education, apprenticeships and professional training. Design/methodology/approach This paper aims to summarise a two-tier project carried out from October 2021 to March 2025. Firstly, a political roadmap was created, afterwards teaching slides, an accompanying text, information material and a website were designed in close connection with stakeholder EPs and graphic designers to lower the hurdle for integrating sustainability aspects in health-care education. Findings The authors demonstrate multiple possibilities for integrating sustainability into education within health care and generated open-access, easy-to-use and freely editable slides, together with an explanatory accompanying text. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Creative tensions in embedding sustainability within higher education: exploring the intersection of sustainability, education and institutional spaces
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore the integration of sustainability into the higher education (HE) curriculum, identifying and examining the key factors that contribute to its successful embedding in educational practice. Design/methodology/approach The paper is based on an institutional case study with a design informed by a systems-based ecological perspective of the university. Case study data includes 19 interviews with educators at varied levels of the university, analysed through thematic coding. Findings The analysis identified three spaces that interact with each other: the sustainability, education and institutional spaces. Discussion is focused on the norms and concepts, processes and structures lying in the intersections between these spaces that are seen as key to the process of embedding sustainability into the curriculum. Originality/value The framing and empirical analysis contribute to discussions of embedding by considering processes beyond curriculum structures, which, whilst important, might be seen as outcomes rather than processes of embedding. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Shared learning spaces as catalysts for the SDGs: a theory of planned behavior study in higher education
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how university shared learning spaces (SLSs) support students to engage in sustainable development goal (SDG)-aligned behaviors. Using the theory of planned behavior it investigates how students’ attitudes (AT), subjective norms (SN) and perceived behavioral control (PBC) predict intentions (IN) and SDG-aligned behaviors (SB) across five domains: SDG 3, 4, 7, 11 and 12. Design/methodology/approach The explanatory mixed-methods design was used, combining confirmatory composite analysis (CCA) for emergent composites within the PLS-SEM framework with survey data from students (n = 364) at a leading Thai public higher education institution (HEI), and Framework Analysis of 15 semi-structured interviews. Findings The model explained 60.6% of variance in IN and 50.7% of variance in SB. IN was the strongest predictor of SB (β = 0.583, p < 0.001), primarily contributed by AT, followed by PBC and SN. PBC also had a smaller direct association with SB. Qualitative findings indicated that sustainability is most evident as co-benefits of students’ daily routines, where norms operate observationally through peers and institutional cues. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The evolving landscape of sustainability competencies: a mixed-methods bibliometric review of ESD scholarship
abstract: Purpose This study aims to map the evolving research landscape of sustainability competencies within Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) by identifying key contributors, examining the intellectual structure of the field and uncovering dominant themes and emerging directions to inform curriculum design, educational policy and future research agendas. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods design was used, combining bibliometric analysis with content analysis. Data comprised 248 articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC, 2021–2025). CiteSpace was used to conduct co-citation, co-authorship and keyword analyses to map collaboration networks, intellectual structures and thematic clusters. Content analysis of highly cited articles provided complementary qualitative depth to validate and contextualize the bibliometric findings. Findings European countries, particularly Spain, occupy central roles in global research collaboration networks, with Sustainability and Journal of Cleaner Production identified as the leading publication venues. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: From textile waste to transformative learning: how infrastructural conditions shape sustainability pedagogy in fashion design education
abstract: Purpose Sustainable fashion education increasingly incorporates sustainability concepts, yet how textile waste (TW) management initiatives and textile recycling (TR) programs are implemented in undergraduate fashion design education remains understudied. This study aims to examine the range of TW/TR initiatives used across fashion programs and explores the factors shaping their pedagogical value and viability. Design/methodology/approach A mixed methods design combined faculty surveys and semistructured interviews across 35 fashion schools in eight countries, an undergraduate student survey, and a participatory action research (PAR) case study implementing a campus TW/TR program at a Canadian university. Findings The study identified three infrastructural configurations: integrated and institutionalized programs, partnership-dependent but fragile programs and grassroots initiatives reliant on individual champions. Across these configurations, pedagogical depth and program viability were shaped less by motivation than by structural support, including budget, defined roles, curricular integration and stable downstream partnerships. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Assessing the impact of SDG education on university students’ benevolence and universalism values
abstract: Purpose The 2030 Agenda establishes 17 sustainable development goals (SDGs) that require coordinated local and global action. The university is a strategic agent for the promotion of values aligned with sustainable development. This study aims to identify if specific activities related to SDGs in university influence not only knowledge but also benevolence and universalism values of Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Values. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected following a pretest-posttest design, at the beginning and end of the 2023–2024 academic year, using an online questionnaire based on Schwartz’s Theory. Between both measurements, professors carried out specific activities related to SGDs. A total of 490 university students participated voluntarily in T1 and 297 in T2. The final sample included 143 students who responded to T1 and T2 (77.6% women, average age: 20.9). journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The development of higher-order thinking skills through case-based curriculum within the framework of sustainable development goals
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the effectiveness of a case-based curriculum developed in the context of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) on prospective teachers’ problem-solving, critical thinking and creative thinking skills. Design/methodology/approach A quasi-experimental pretest–post-test non-equivalent control group design with an embedded written qualitative feedback component was used. Findings This study results revealed that prospective teachers in the experimental group showed a significant increase in their critical thinking, problem-solving and creative thinking skills, and that their critical thinking and problem-solving skills were significantly higher than those of prospective teachers in the control group. The Written Feedback Form on SDGs indicated that prospective teachers developed a more multidimensional understanding of the SDGs and reported reconsidering some everyday practices. Research limitations/implications First, this study was conducted at a single institution with a modest total sample (n = 49). Second, the intervention lasted eight weeks. Third, the quasi-experimental design is vulnerable to limitations associated with single-site studies.

journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Pathways towards net-zero university campuses: a systemic design and simulation
abstract: Purpose University campuses serve as critical testbeds for net-zero transitions, but campus decarbonization measures are often designed and assessed in isolation, with limited attention to the dynamic interactions among energy, buildings, human activities and emissions. This study aims to propose a four-in-one analytical framework that differentiates the functional roles of energy substitution, infrastructure efficiency, organizational capacity and carbon-feedback regulation in campus operational decarbonization. Design/methodology/approach To explore these dynamics, an integrated system dynamics model is developed for a stylized, average-scale Chinese university campus. Scenario simulations from 2025 to 2035 compare a baseline pathway, four single-lever interventions and a coordinated intervention package. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The impact of a green chemistry and alternative energy course on science teacher students’ sustainability attitudes and self-reported environmental behavior
abstract: Purpose Green chemistry education is widely recognized as essential for equipping future science educators with the knowledge, values and competencies needed to address global sustainability challenges. Nevertheless, dedicated green chemistry courses within preservice teacher education remain rare, particularly in the Israeli higher education context. This study aims to examine the impact of a course titled Green Chemistry and Alternative Energy on preservice science teachers’ sustainability attitudes, environmental behavior, interest in chemistry and pedagogical readiness. Design/methodology/approach An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was used. In total, 53 third-year Chemistry–Biology B.Ed. students at a teacher training college in northern Israel participated in a quasi-experimental pre–post study. Quantitative data were collected via two validated questionnaires, a 24-item sustainability attitudes scale (a = 0.95) and a 19-item chemistry interest scale (a = 0.81), administered before and after the 26-h semester course. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Bridging sustainable development goals (SDGs) and career awareness through the implementation of a coaching-based career planning course
abstract: Purpose The aim of this study is to examine the effects of a coaching-based career planning course on students’ career awareness and to discuss the findings in the context of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 (Quality Education) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 110 students enrolled at Çukurova University. The study employed an explanatory sequential mixed method design consisting of two stages. The first stage was conducted as a quasi-experimental study with repeated measures between September 2024 and June 2025. The second stage took place one semester later (the fall semester) and was designed using thematic analysis, a qualitative research method. Both stages were conducted face-to-face. Findings According to the findings, the coaching-based educational intervention had a positive and statistically meaningful effect on students’ career awareness (p < 0.05). However, a single coaching-based course is not equally effective across all dimensions of career awareness. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: From participation to transformation: mapping collaborative pathways to sustainability in UK higher education
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how collaboration is enacted within sustainability agendas in UK higher education, positioning it as the mechanism through which sustainability integration is realised. Building on the Sustainability Integration Framework, it interrogates the gap between policy rhetoric and institutional practice through critical discourse analysis of policies and practitioner interviews. It develops a Collaboration Continuum – participation, collaboration, co-creation and transformation – to explain how agency, decision-making authority and resources are distributed. Findings show collaboration is often consultative and voluntary, limiting power redistribution. The paper identifies enabling conditions for deeper integration and offers a governance lens for achieving embedded, equitable, whole-institution sustainability practice. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a qualitative design using critical discourse analysis of eight institutional sustainability policies and semi-structured interviews with staff across diverse UK higher education institutions (HEIs). journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The guiding effect of green governance in higher education institutions on students’ environmental behaviors
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore how green governance in higher education institutions influences students’ environmental behaviors, with a particular focus on bridging the “intention–behavior gap.” It investigates the direct effect of green governance and the mediating roles of responsibility and group norms. Design/methodology/approach A questionnaire survey was conducted among 1,010 university students. Structural equation modeling, Bootstrap mediation tests and Welch ANOVA with Games–Howell post hoc comparisons were used to test the proposed model and group differences. Findings Green governance in higher education institutions significantly promotes students’ environmental behaviors. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Education for sustainable development through waste valorisation research projects: training sustainability competencies in agro-industrial engineering students during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how education for sustainable development (ESD) can be effectively implemented within higher education institutions through authentic waste valorisation research projects, even under the challenging circumstances of the COVID-19 pandemic. This study demonstrates how final-degree projects (FDPs) focused on circular economy principles can develop key sustainability competencies in agro-industrial engineering students while contributing to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 4 and 12. We analyse how integrating problem-based learning, project-based learning, learning-by-doing and research-based learning approaches creates synergistic effects for competency development. Design/methodology/approach A multiple-case study methodology was used to analyse three FDPs focused on agro-industrial waste valorisation (coffee residues, goat milk whey and cocoa pod husks) conducted between March 2020 and March 2022 at a public university in Ecuador. Quantitative data from 229 graduates across seven engineering programmes were integrated with qualitative analyses of pedagogical strategies and competency development indicators. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The food waste–food insecurity nexus in higher education: a review with evidence from African universities
abstract: Purpose This study examines the global literature on the relationship between food waste and food insecurity in higher education institutions (HEIs), with an emphasis on Sub-Saharan African contexts. It develops a theory of planned behaviour (TPB)-grounded conceptual framework for the food waste–food insecurity nexus in African HEIs. It identifies evidence-based intervention pathways aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2 and 12. Design/methodology/approach Following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 43 quality-assured peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2026 were systematically identified, screened and thematically synthesised from a broader bibliometric corpus of 63 studies. Bibliometric analysis examined publication trends, key contributors, geographic concentration, journal outlets and keyword co-occurrence patterns using VOSviewer analytical conventions. Thematic synthesis followed Thomas and Harden’s (2008) three-stage procedure. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Impact of aesthetic music education philosophy on early childhood teachers’ professional identity: an exploratory mixed-methods perspective on SDG 4
abstract: Purpose The professional identity of early childhood teachers plays a crucial role in improving teaching quality, job satisfaction and children’s holistic development. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the impact of integrating aesthetic music education into early childhood teachers’ lesson planning and its influence on their professional identity while contributing to SDG 4 – quality education. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was used, with qualitative inquiry as the primary focus. Quantitative data were collected through a survey of 200 early childhood teachers to assess overall levels of professional identity and aesthetic music education role identity, providing contextual support for the study. Qualitative data were gathered through lesson-planning observations, semistructured interviews and analysis of planning records from ten teachers with diverse backgrounds to examine teachers’ perceptions, experiences and challenges in practice. Findings Results indicate that aesthetic music education enhances teachers’ professional identity, shifting their role from “knowledge transmitters” to “aesthetic guides,” improving their sense of professional mission

journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Beyond mitigation agendas: climate adaptation, institutional responses and resilience in higher education institutions facing extreme climate events
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how higher education institutions (HEIs) adapt and respond to extreme climate events and identify the climate resilience approaches reported in the literature. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review following the Knowledge Development Process–Constructivist (ProKnow-C) protocol was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science databases. After applying eligibility criteria, 34 articles were selected and analyzed through descriptive and systemic approaches. Findings Institutional responses are heterogeneous. Reactive and incremental approaches predominate, whereas planned and collaborative strategies are associated with stronger adaptive capacity. Climate resilience is conceptualized as an institutional process, a measurable performance outcome or an infrastructural attribute. Research limitations/implications The review was limited to the portfolio selection phase of the ProKnow-C protocol and reflects a predominance of studies from Global North contexts. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Universities as living laboratories for circular economy: curriculum-integrated agroforestry as environmental management in higher education
abstract: Purpose This article aims to examine how curriculum-integrated circular economy (CE) practices can function as an environmental management mechanism within higher education institutions (HEIs). It argues that the academic curriculum, when tightly coupled with operational infrastructure, can serve as a form of institutional “soft governance” that orchestrates circular resource flows across teaching, research and community engagement. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, single embedded case study methodology is used, conceptualised through a living laboratory (LL) framework. The case is the “Passionfruit Commercialization Project” initiative at an Australian branch campus university in Sarawak, Malaysia. Two embedded units of analysis are examined: (1) a faculty-led agroforestry trial plot functioning as an upstream environmental production system, and (2) a formally integrated final-year Business Consulting Project unit involving 30 undergraduate business students organised into six teams. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The effects of learning experience on education for sustainable development in general education from the students’ perspectives
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the effects of learning experience on education for sustainable development (ESD) in general education (GE) from students’ perspectives. Referring to the Sustainable Development Goals-related GE (SDG-GE) courses at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, the effects of learning experience on the ESD learning outcomes of learning attitude, knowledge acquisition and reflection, and action are investigated, along with the reasons behind these effects. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-method approach was used in this study. Quantitative analysis served as the first and dominant strand. Data was collected from a questionnaire survey and analyzed using Student’s t-test and structural equation modeling (SEM). Qualitative analysis served as the second strand. Data was collected from student focus group interviews. Findings This study shows that learning experience in SDG-GE is positively associated with students’ learning attitude, knowledge acquisition and reflection and action. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Green HRM and STARA capabilities in higher education: the mediating roles of green innovation and green passion in sustainable performance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) and Smart Technology–AI–Robotics–Algorithms (STARA) capabilities operate as concurrent human- and digital-capability domains associated with sustainable performance in higher education institutions (HEIs). It further tests whether green innovation (GI) and green passion (GP) explain these relationships as parallel mediating mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Using a three-wave, one-month time-lagged survey of employees from 10 HEIs in Sindh, Pakistan, this study analysed 424 matched responses. Hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Predictive performance was assessed using PLSpredict and complementary machine-learning models, with SHAP used for predictive interpretation. Findings Both GHRM and STARA capabilities are positively associated with sustainable performance, and GI and GP each significantly mediate these relationships. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Curricular integration of the sustainable development goals in nursing education: evidence from the Universidad Técnica del Norte (Ecuador)
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine how the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are integrated into a nursing education program at the Universidad Técnica del Norte (UTN), Ecuador and to identify the institutional, curricular and pedagogical factors associated with their explicit incorporation. The study aims to clarify the gap between SDGs awareness and formal curricular enactment in higher education for the health sciences. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a sequential mixed-methods design combining qualitative, quantitative and documentary approaches. Data were collected through a faculty focus group, surveys administered to instructors (n = 35) and undergraduate nursing students (n = 498) and a microcurricular review of official course syllabi (n = 45) within the UTN nursing program. Quantitative analyses included nonparametric tests, correlation analyses, clustering techniques and logistic regression, while qualitative and documentary data were integrated through methodological triangulation. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Digital pathways to sustainability engagement in higher education: the sequential role of social media, awareness, and attitudes
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how social media platform use is associated with sustainability engagement among university students by investigating the sequential mediating roles of sustainability awareness and sustainability attitudes. Grounded in social cognitive theory (SCT) and the knowledge–attitude–practices (KAP) framework, the study aims to explain how digitally mediated sustainability communication is linked to sustainable consumption and pro-environmental behaviour within higher education. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was used using survey data collected from undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in Jordanian public universities. A total of 867 valid responses were obtained using a non-probability convenience sampling approach with voluntary participation. Measurement items were adapted from established scales and assessed using a five-point Likert scale. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS to evaluate the measurement model and test the proposed sequential mediation model. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Investigation of plastic-bottled, tap and filtered water: university students’ preference, identification and reported usage
abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess a university community’s reported usage and identification of, and preference for filtered (via public “hydration station”), single-use bottled water (SUBW) and tap water. Design/methodology/approach A double-blind, randomized taste-test experiment was conducted at a mid-size (approximately 7,700 students) university in the USA. Participants also completed a brief survey assessing beverage and container usage in the past week. Findings Of 112 participants, most preferred filtered water and commercial bottled water more than tap water. Overall, participants were most accurate in identifying tap water and least accurate with bottled water. For most preferred water, participants accurately identified tap water to a significant degree. Overall, participants’ taste preference for filtered water agreed with their self-report of high refillable bottle of filtered water usage. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Perceptions of Brazilian technological education students on photovoltaic systems in schools: impact on learning and sustainability promotion
abstract: Purpose Since 2014, the Brazilian Ministry of Education has promoted the use of renewable energy in the Federal Technological Education Network (FNTE) with the objective of enhancing sustainability practices and integrating knowledge into the teaching–learning process. The IF Solar Project was developed to extend the benefits of photovoltaic energy beyond mere economic savings and incorporate it into educational activities. This research study aims to examine students’ perceptions of photovoltaics at the Federal Institute of Rio Grande do Norte (IFRN), with the objective of identifying actions that can be implemented to strengthen its role in the learning process. Design/methodology/approach The research design used a survey–based quantitative approach, using a structured questionnaire administered to students across multiple campuses. A survey was conducted with 11,888 students, using 461 questionnaires across 20 IFRN campuses, with a 5% margin of error and a 95% confidence level. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Sense of gain of biodiversity in Chinese university campuses: influence mechanism, current status and improvement directions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the mechanism by which the public’s sense of gain (SG) from campus biodiversity is shaped and to establish an evaluative model thereof. Design/methodology/approach A total of 932 samples were collected from Chinese universities. Structural equation modeling was used to verify the proposed influence paths among the four constructs. A fuzzy synthetic evaluation model was then developed to assess the current status and identify directions for improvement. Findings The social governance system (GOV), the content of gain (CG) and the way of gain (WG) significantly influence the SG. Although a strong SG was reported (grade = 5.014 on a seven-point scale), several areas require improvement. The highly rated CG (grade = 5.220) requires improvements to the water environment. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Life cycle and behavioral analysis of single-use research laboratory plastic recycling on a college campus
abstract: Purpose University research laboratories generate large volumes of single-use plastics, particularly polypropylene (PP) research waste (e.g. pipette tips). While reduction and reuse strategies remain the preferred actions within the circular economy hierarchy (e.g. 10R/3R: reduce, reuse, recycle), these are rarely feasible at scale in laboratory environments without workflow redesign and education. This study aims to examine the technical, environmental, behavioral and implementation feasibility of a decentralized recycling system within an engineering department in a higher education research setting. Design/methodology/approach This study presents a department-wide survey of engineering researchers to assess usage patterns, barriers and adoption attitudes. This study describes a pilot recycling process implemented on campus at a public university in Texas, USA. This process recycles non-hazardous research plastics (i.e. pipette tips) by collecting, shredding and injecting the materials into molds to create new lab products. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: An analysis of Taiwan’s educational contributions to sustainable development: evidence from Taiwan’s university social responsibility
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the operational logic through which Taiwan’s university social responsibility (USR) program, led by the Taiwan authorities, promotes local sustainable development, compare it with the operational logic of USR programs in Europe and the United States, and further propose policy recommendations for different USR models. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative research approach, including case studies, semi-structured interviews, secondary data analysis and comparative analysis, to systematically examine the operational logic of Taiwan’s USR program across multiple dimensions, including governance structures, curricular mechanisms, community participation, resource integration, outcome generation and sustainability. This study sample consisted of two highly representative local USR cases, along with interview data from nine key actors, including project planners, faculty, students and community collaborators associated with these cases. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: COIL+: integrating experiential and blended learning to advance soft skills and global competence in sustainability education
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how a STEM-contextualized and Education for Sustainable Development-oriented international co-learning model (COIL+) cultivates soft skills and global competence among agricultural undergraduates in Japan and South Korea – two East Asian countries selected for their shared rural demographic pressures and comparable small-scale agricultural structures. Design/methodology/approach The authors implemented a convergent mixed-methods design across three program iterations (FY2022–FY2024). Anonymous post-program surveys (n = 21 of 51 enrolled; 41.2% response rate) captured self-reported gains in leadership, teamwork, problem-solving, communication and creativity. Three focus groups (n = 9) at four and nine months after program participation explored learning mechanisms and temporal trajectories. Quantitative analyses included descriptive statistics, internal-consistency testing and within-participant non-parametric tests; qualitative data underwent six-step thematic analysis with dual coding. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Bridging the efficiency gap in the dual transition of higher education through digital maturity and strategic governance
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the strategic alignment between digital transformation and environmental sustainability in higher education institutions. Addressing the “siloed” management of these domains, this paper aims to determine whether digitalization is governed merely as an operational tool for control or as a systemic catalyst for closing the “efficiency gap” between institutional intent and environmental performance. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a qualitative multiple case study approach, this research uses a purposive maximum variation sampling strategy to analyze the strategic plans (2020–2030) of four Spanish universities with distinct institutional logics. A thematic content analysis was conducted using a hybrid deductive-inductive coding matrix, ensuring that theoretical grounding in quality assurance and financial sustainability is enriched by empirical discovery. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: The relation between sustainability and campus layouts: a comparative international case study of three universities
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to explore the relationship between campus layouts of three universities in different countries of the world and environmental, economic and social sustainability. Design/methodology/approach The study uses ethnographic approach to the study of the central phenomenon of interest – the interplay between campus spatial layout and economic, environmental and social sustainability. The main approach to data collection in this study was participant observation. Findings The study reveals that the compact form of the layout, the smaller size, the extent of isolation of the campus from the rest of the city and the size of the city and the level of development of the city’s public transportation are related to higher levels of sustainability. Research limitations/implications The findings are context-specific and based on qualitative data, which limits generalizability. The differing missions and national contexts of the universities studied may also influence outcomes. Future research using standardized metrics across similar institutions is recommended. Practical implications Results can guide university planners in designing more sustainable campuses

journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Integrating AI in environmental education: a quality-focused framework for higher education institutions in emerging markets
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to propose a five-stage, quality-focused framework to guide higher education institutions in emerging markets through the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into environmental education. It addresses a gap that existing frameworks have not filled: how institutions operating under resource constraints can adopt AI tools while preserving the experiential, place-based and community-connected foundations on which environmental pedagogy depends. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on experiential learning theory, education for sustainable development principles and comparative quality assurance research, this conceptual study synthesises literature across AI in education, environmental pedagogy and institutional quality systems. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: From learning to action: transformative pedagogies driving SDG-oriented entrepreneurship in higher education
abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyze how project-based learning (PBL) in higher education entrepreneurship courses contributes to the development of sustainable entrepreneurial competencies and to students’ social and environmental commitment, highlighting its relevance to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Design/methodology/approach A pre–post design was applied to a sample of undergraduate students enrolled in a “Business Creation” course. Students worked on entrepreneurial projects using PBL. Data were collected using validated scales of sustainable entrepreneurial competences and social and environmental commitment. Findings Results show significant improvements in all sustainable entrepreneurial competencies after the training experience. Students reported high levels of social and environmental commitment, particularly regarding equity, employment protection, sustainability training and green marketing. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Exploring empowerment of rural women entrepreneurs through technical and vocational education and training (TVET): an inclusive development perspective
abstract: Purpose In light of the vulnerability of women, this paper aims to establish how technical and vocational education and training (TVET) education empowers rural entrepreneurial women through the adoption of information and communication technology (ICT). Worryingly, access to TVET remains elusive to several entrepreneurial women living in poor rural communities in Zimbabwe. Scarcity of literature that approaches TVET from an inclusive development perspective motivated the current study. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted an interpretative paradigm that advocates for a qualitative approach. In accordance with an exploratory research design, data collected from 17 rural entrepreneurial women by means of interviews and observations were analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings The results revealed that digital TVET can help entrepreneurial rural women in terms of economic empowerment (SDG 8), poverty elimination (SDG 1), skills development (SDG 4), innovation (SDG 9), rural development (SDG 8) and stimulating entrepreneurial culture (SDG 8). journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Development and validation of a questionnaire for measuring awareness of campus sustainability among students and faculty members
abstract: Purpose Most previous studies have focused on university management practices and the measures taken to transform higher education institutions into green university campuses, without sufficiently addressing tools to assess campus sustainability awareness. This study aims to fill this gap by developing and validating a reliable tool to assess student and faculty awareness of campus sustainability standards. Design/methodology/approach Face-to-face survey responses were collected from 650 students and faculty members in 18 faculties at Cairo University, Egypt. The initial questionnaire consisted of 40 items and underwent face and content validity. Construct validity was assessed using exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis and reliability analysis was evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha. Findings The final tool consisted of 33 items and revealed a three-factor structure, explaining more than 45% of the total variance. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Student sustainability trade-offs in higher education: how green consumption values relate to willingness to accept sustainability-related environmental costs
abstract: Purpose Accepting environmental sustainability costs is a recurring constraint in sustainable consumption and higher education, where students are increasingly exposed to sustainability-related trade-offs and cost-bearing measures. This study aims to examine how green consumption values (GCVs) and consciousness for sustainable consumption (CSC) relate to willingness to accept environmental sustainability costs (WAEs) among Polish Generation Z university students, and whether the GCV-WAE and CSC-WAE associations differ by gender. Design/methodology/approach The study analyses cross-sectional CAWI survey data from Polish Generation Z higher education students (n = 1,474) using structural equation modelling. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Learning for life and sustainability: a theory synthesis to sustainability mindset development in higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore the synthesis of transformative learning (TL) with curricular nuances and autonomy-supportive learning to develop sustainability mindsets in higher education institutions (HEIs), particularly in teacher education programs, in support of Agenda2030. By situating this exploration within a lifelong learning (LLL) perspective, the paper highlights the importance of fostering sustainability mindsets across the lifespan. Design/methodology/approach Jaakkola’s (2020) theory synthesis design was implemented. During the synthesis, similarities in approaches and learning strategies for sustainability were identified and integrated into a comprehensive framework, indicating how these theories/concepts interact. Findings Evident links exist among these theories/concepts for sustainability mindset development. By highlighting their synergies, the paper proposes a conceptual framework for sustainability mindset development grounded in LLL that prepares individuals of all ages to address global challenges effectively. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: An empirical exploration of a business school’s effect on students’ sustainability mindsets
abstract: Purpose Aligned with the United Nation’s Principles of Responsible Management Education, business schools are expected to incorporate sustainability education in their curriculum with an implicit assumption that graduates practice these values beyond university. This paper aims to challenge this assumption by investigating whether and how students’ sustainability values and attitudes are developed in business schools through identity theory. Design/methodology/approach The authors used a two-stage parallel mixed methods design in this study. Stage 1 used a quantitative, two-wave longitudinal survey, assessing students’ sustainability attitudes before and after completing a sustainability-focused course in 2021, 2022 and 2023. Stage 2 used qualitative, semistructured in-depth interviews to examine graduates’ sustainability values while at university, during their transition to employment, and in the early stages of graduate employment. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: An integrated design framework for sustainability-focused micro-credentials in higher education
abstract: Purpose Micro-credentials are increasingly positioned within European higher education as flexible learning pathways that support the digital and green transitions while widening access, equity and lifelong learning. This paper aims to examine the design and evaluation of sustainability-focused micro-credentials using an integrated model combining Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation (ADDIE), ABC Learning Design and GreenComp: The European Sustainability Competence Framework. Design/methodology/approach This small-scale practice evaluation was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 adopted a design-based approach to examine the collaborative instructional design process undertaken by the research team as practitioner-designers. Phase 2 piloted the evaluation of learners’ self-reported sustainability competences within a single sustainability-focused micro-credential using a post-module survey that asked participants to retrospectively rate their perceived competences before and after completing the module. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Environmental sustainability and climate action plans in higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose This systematic review aims to synthesize existing knowledge on climate action plans (CAPs) in higher education institutions (HEIs) to establish a comprehensive framework for institutional climate strategies. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic review methodology, this paper analyzes 22 academic articles on CAPs in HEIs. The analysis categorized findings into five major themes: energy and infrastructure; climate action planning and strategy; education, research and student engagement; community and policy engagement; and transportation. Findings A primary finding is the categorization of efforts into five major themes that facilitate organized institutional research. A secondary, critical finding identifies ten core areas of action, ranging from energy management to equity and justice, that expand CAPs from a narrow carbon-accounting tool to a holistic institutional roadmap. title: Sustainable campus liveability in residential technical institutions: a quantitative framework supporting the UN SDGs
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop and empirically validate a context-specific framework for assessing campus liveability in Indian residential technical institutions. The framework was designed to advance sustainable development in higher education, directly supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs) 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing), 4 (Quality Education) and 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods research design was adopted, combining a Delphi process, survey-based data collection across three leading Indian technical campuses and advanced quantitative analysis. A factor structure was established through exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and user priorities were identified using an importance–satisfaction analysis. Findings Seven key dimensions of campus liveability were confirmed: residential quality, sociocultural vibrancy, support services, safety and security, amenities, environmental quality and accessibility/mobility. title: Digital intelligence technologies and environmental governance in universities: a China-Arab comparative study
abstract: Purpose This study focuses on universities in China and Arab countries. title: Digital incentives and behavioral feedback: a study on the targeted intervention mechanism for municipal waste separation in Shanghai universities
abstract: Purpose This study examines municipal waste separation practices in Shanghai universities, with the aim of exploring how digital incentives and real-time feedback mechanisms influence waste-sorting behaviors among faculty and students. It seeks to identify the behavioral impact pathways of different incentive designs and feedback types, and to clarify the psychological and institutional conditions under which digital interventions can promote sustained participation and compliance in campus environmental governance. Design/methodology/approach This study develops a theoretical framework integrating technology design, psychological mechanisms, behavioral outcomes and institutional context. A mixed-methods research design is used, including questionnaire surveys (n = 1,287), system log data from 812 users, in-depth interviews and field observations across three representative Shanghai universities. Hypotheses are systematically tested to assess the effects of social and material incentives, feedback mechanisms and contextual factors on waste separation behavior. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Eco-efficiency and financial sustainability in UK universities: strategic pathways to a carbon-neutral higher education sector
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to assess the eco-efficiency of universities in the UK and investigate the impact of critical financial indicators on environmental performance. This is particularly relevant in the context of institutions that are seeking to balance financial sustainability with climate commitments. Design/methodology/approach Using data from the entire population of 160 British higher education institutions from 2015 to 2021, a two-stage empirical methodology is implemented. Institutional eco-efficiency is evaluated through Data Envelopment Analysis during the initial phase. Quantile regression analysis is used in the second stage to examine the impact of financial indicators, such as profitability, liquidity and operational cash flow, on eco-efficiency across various performance quantiles. title: Designing a sustainable leadership model to enhance administrative competencies for implementing ESD principles in Jordanian universities: a fuzzy Delphi approach
abstract: Purpose This study aims to respond to the pressing need for leadership frameworks that support education for sustainable development (ESD) in higher education. In Jordanian universities, structural and governance constraints hinder effective ESD integration, necessitating a context-specific leadership model. Design/methodology/approach A two-round Fuzzy Delphi Method was used to identify and prioritise essential components of the sustainable leadership model. Round 1 established expert consensus on key elements, while Round 2 ranked their relevance to refine the model’s structure. Findings The final model comprises five dimensions: self, university community, educational integration, sustainability governance and sustainability partnerships. High-priority items highlight the role of ethical leadership, stakeholder empowerment, integrated planning and cross-sector collaboration in driving institutional change. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Digital feedback and waste separation behaviour in university sport venues: a multi-method investigation of environmental innovation in higher education infrastructure
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether digital feedback interventions can change spectator waste separation behaviour in university sport venues and how social influence processes amplify these effects, contributing to the broader understanding of environmental management innovations within higher education institutions. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 4,847 spectators at a university arena in Shanghai across 312 events over 18 months (September 2023 to February 2025). The intervention consisted of a mobile application and digital displays providing real-time waste separation feedback. Agent-based modelling simulated social influence processes within spectator populations. Findings Waste separation rates increased from 22.3% to 61.2% (p < 0.001, d = 1.82). Environmental identity scores rose 11.9% (p < 0.001, d = 0.48). Undergraduate students showed the largest improvement (+219%) despite lowest baseline rates. Agent-based simulations revealed that 54% of total effects resulted from social influence rather than direct feedback exposure, with each environmentally engaged spectator influencing 2.3 additional individuals. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: Higher education green innovation and regional digitalization: spatiotemporal evolution and drivers
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how higher education green innovation (HEGI) and regional digital development (RDD) evolve across Chinese provinces, how their spatial inequality changes and which regional conditions are associated with stronger coordination. Design/methodology/approach Using provincial panel data for China from 2014 to 2023, this study applies improved entropy-weighted TOPSIS, a revised coupling coordination degree model, Dagum Gini decomposition, the standard deviational ellipse, a two-way fixed-effects Spatial Durbin Model and a supplementary reduced-instrument System GMM model. Findings Coordination between HEGI and RDD increased steadily from near imbalance to primary coordination. Spatial inequality declined overall, although an east-west gradient remained and inter-regional differences were still the main source of disparity. Economic development and industrial upgrading were positively associated with local coordination and positive spillovers, whereas urban congestion and the pollution-haven channel of environmental regulation constrained coordination. journal_name: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
title: University students’ climate resilience: the roles of scientific consensus messaging, trust in science, and climate change attitudes
abstract: Purpose The social capital of science has eroded globally, as reflected in the growing criticism of scientific expertise and increasingly ambivalent public attitudes. Events such as the 2011 Fukushima tsunami and nuclear crisis further undermined trust in science. In the post-truth era, climate politics, misinformation and the inherent uncertainties of climate science have made it even more difficult for the public to appropriately understand scientific evidence despite scientists’ collective efforts to communicate the urgency of climate action. This study aims to investigate how university students’ perceptions of scientific consensus and trust in science shape their attitudes toward climate change. Design/methodology/approach A survey was conducted on 394 university students to gather data on their environmental and climatic attitudes. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to test the hypothesized relationships. Findings The results showed that scientific consensus messaging and trust in science influenced students’ climate attitudes through distinct psychological pathways, including effects on climate risk perception and knowledge.
